text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Austrian newspapers.
- German tyre maker Continental threatens to cut production even further in its Austrian Semperit plant if workers go ahead with plans to fight major job cuts.
- Finance Minister Viktor Klima said in Washington he would present the new tender for bids for Creditanstalt next week.
- Privatisation of aluminium maker Amag, a unit of OeIAG, has been postponed.
- Bank Austria chief Gerhard Randa said at the World Bank meeting in Washington, that three schemes for privatising the government's 17 percent stake in his bank are being evaluated.
- "The never-ending story of the CA privatisation will be clearly decided and finished by the end of the year", Viktor Klima said in Washington.
- Austrian electricity supplier Verbund said it expected to save around one billion schillings by cutting 650 jobs and restructuring.
- A simplified and deregulated law for the creation of new firms should help to create more jobs, Trade Minister Johann Farnleitner said.
- Austria's Finance Minister said he was against selling IMF gold reserves to help developing countries.
- Austrian papermaker Leykam's main share holder, Dutch KNP B.T., wants to reduce its stake in Leykam.
- Wolfgang Bachmayer, top candidate of the Liberal Forum at the October 13 Vienna elections, resigned after being criticised for racist remarks made in 1991.
- Bank Austria said in Washington it would welcome a foreign partner for its privatisation.
- Tourism revenues are to drop even further in 1997 after a very poor summer this year, research institute IHS expects.
